newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Two killed in South Africa ahead of Zulu march.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in South Africa ahead of Zulu march.

text.p: Two men were killed in Soweto township on Wednesday ahead of a march called by Zulu nationalists to commemorate the deaths of more than 50 people in a demonstration three years ago, South African police said.

About 12,000 marchers, most of them in traditional Zulu dress and carrying spears, sticks and leather-bound shields, began their five kilometre (three miles) march to the Library Gardens, in the heart of Johannesburg, where they planned to hold a service in memory of those who died.
The march, led by eight police vehicles, was closely watched by armed police and main intersections were blocked by armoured vehicles.
Razor wire protected the front of the headquarters of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC), where eight Zulu demonstrators were killed by security guards during the 1994 march.
Organisers said the march was not only to remember the dead, but was also a call on the government to declare the day a public holiday.

At least 55 people were killed and hundreds injured in and around Johannesburg during the demonstration in 1994 when supporters of the mainly Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party marched in support of Zulu King Goodwill Zwelithini.
The march came a month ahead of the country's first all-race elections, which Inkatha had vowed to boycott. The party later agreed to take part in the vote.
Mandela told parliament months later that he had ordered security guards to protect the ANC building against any attack.
The attorney-general launched a probe into the shootings, but no one has yet been prosecuted.

Police spokesman Superintendent Govindsamy Mariemuthoo said trouble erupted in the early hours on Wednesday around a Zulu workers' hostels in Soweto, the giant sprawling township southwest of the city, as well as in some areas to the east of Johannesburg where roads were blocked.
Shots were fired at various hostels in Soweto and roads were barricaded with rocks. Two people were wounded in separate shootings near the hostels and two buses were burnt.
There were also reports of intimidation, where people had been ordered to join the march.
The violence was believed to be linked to the demonstration, he said, adding that police had warned the public to stay away from the city centre on Wednesday.
Financial market traders expressed concern about the two deaths ahead of the march.
They said news of the killings had weakened the rand and bond markets and hoped the march would pass off peacefully before Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget speech at 1215 GMT.
